citation.publication: Kohn, M.S., Mast, M.A., and Gross, T.A., 2026, Peak-, mean-, and low-streamflow regional-regression equations for natural streamflow in central and western Colorado, 2019: U.S. Geological Survey Scientific Investigations Report 2025-5047

notes: NOT a flowfreq-developed set: this is a USGS publication, Kohn, Mast and Gross, SIR 2025-5047 (published 2026; pubs page revised 2026-05-18), stored under provisional/ only so that it is opt-in (load_state('CO', allow_provisional=True)) while NSS/StreamStats still serve the 2009/2016/2006 equations in CO.json (NSS citations 20, 21 and 11). The generic provisional advisory that load_state attaches ('developed by flowfreq ... not reviewed or published by the USGS') is therefore inaccurate for this file; this note is authoritative. Scope: peak-flow equations only (Table 1, pp. 20-22): GLS (WREG) regressions for the 2-, 5-, 10-, 25-, 50-, 100-, 200- and 500-year peaks (AEP 0.5-0.002) in four hydrologic regions defined by mean basin elevation (ft NAVD 88): Alpine > 10,490 (105 gages), Sub-Alpine 9,493-10,490 (104), Mid-Elevation 8,015-9,492 (104), Plateau < 8,014 (105); 418 gages through WY2019, none used in two regions. The region is chosen from the basin's mean elevation, not from a map (p. 9), so the regions have no geographic boundaries; flowfreq does not select the region, the caller does. The report's boundaries leave 1-ft gaps (8,014-8,015 and 9,492-9,493) and put exactly 10,490 ft in Sub-Alpine. NSS's staging draft (below) instead uses ALTELEV >= 10490 Alpine, [9492, 10490) Sub-Alpine, [8014, 9492) Mid-Elevation, < 8014 Plateau. The mean-annual, mean-monthly, 7-day minimum and maximum and flow-duration equations (Tables 2-5) and the drainage-area-ratio exponents (Table 6) are not stored. Form: each equation is printed as Q = 10^b0 AREA^b1 10^(c1*X1 + c2*X2 [+ c3*X3]) (eq. 5); DRNAREA is the only log10-transformed predictor and every other variable enters untransformed (transform identity), exactly as printed. Variable codes are the StreamStats codes printed in Table 1's 'approximate range' row: AREA = DRNAREA (mi2); LONG = LONG_CENT (longitude of basin centroid, decimal degrees NAD 83, negative west); SLOPE = BSLDEM10M (mean basin slope, percent, from 1/3 arc-second 3DEP); MEANELEV = ELEV (mean basin elevation, ft NAVD 88); SWE = APR1_SWE (April 1 snow-water equivalent, in.; Table 1.2 lists the SNODAS April 1 SWE in meters but Table 1's range 0-33.8 is in inches, and NSS's staging draft uses inches); P100Y24H/100Y24H = I24H100Y (24-hour, 100-year precipitation, in.; NOAA Atlas 2/14); PPTANN = PRECIP (mean annual precipitation, in., 800-m PRISM). The Sub-Alpine rows print the 24-hour variable as P100Y24H and the Plateau rows as 100Y24H; the header defines one variable, 100Y24H. NSS's staging draft names four of these differently, ALTBSLDEM, ALTELEV, ALI24H100Y and PRECPRIS10 (DRNAREA, LONG_CENT and APR1_SWE are the same), which suggests StreamStats will compute 'alternate' versions of slope, elevation and the 100-year rainfall for these equations; the report's own codes are stored. Limits: the report publishes one pooled 'approximate range of predictor variables' for all four regions (Table 1 headnote), and those pooled ranges are stored on every equation, as NSS's staging draft also uses them. Per-region ranges are not published (the data release, doi:10.5066/P9Q5AMFV, is 'Under Revision' and unavailable as of 2026-10-13). Table 1.1's per-gage drainage areas give the per-region spans Alpine 0.89-1,310, Sub-Alpine 0.76-1,450, Mid-Elevation 1.79-17,100 and Plateau 0.22-22,600 mi2 (five Alpine/Sub-Alpine gages list #N/A), so the pooled DRNAREA limit of 22,629 mi2 is far outside what the Alpine and Sub-Alpine fits saw; extrapolation warnings will not catch that. Error statistics: sep_log is Table 1's SEP (percent, the square root of the mean GLS variance of prediction, p. 13) converted as sqrt(ln(1 + (SEP/100)^2)) / ln(10); model_error_variance is the SME (standard model error, percent) converted the same way and squared, the convention CO.json uses for SIR 2009-5136. No AVP beyond the SEP and no covariance matrix (X'L^-1X)^-1 is printed; the report says the final regression models are in the data release, which is unavailable, so intervals fall back to sep_log. pseudo-R2 is not stored (Table 1 prints it). n_sites is Table 1's N, and Table 1.1's per-gage region column gives the same counts. Area-weighting (p. 32): for a basin in two regions the report weights the flows (not their logs) by drainage-area fraction; use evaluate_weighted(..., space='linear'). Double entry: the stored values were parsed from the report's JATS XML (MathML) and checked against an independent parse of the PDF text layer (intercepts, all coefficients, N, pseudo-R2 and SEP for all 32 equations, and the SME column in order), with zero disagreements, and are typed a third time in tests/test_regression_colorado_2025.py. The report prints no worked example and no per-gage regression estimates, so the evaluation cross-check is against NSS's staging draft of this report (test.streamstats.usgs.gov, citation 200, regions 995-998, status 'Review', not public in NSS or StreamStats), whose equation strings match Table 1 term for term and whose returned values (3 significant figures) at two input sets per region the stored equations reproduce.
